issue: The segment exhibit doesn't reconcile with the consolidated data, and it doesn't give the external revenue that the 75% test cited in the s5 rationale needs.
evidence: Segment revenue (external + intersegment) totals 1,700 + 700 + 250 + 200 + 150 = 3,000 ($000s), exactly equal to consolidated net sales of 3,000,000, which implies zero intersegment revenue despite the column heading. Segment profit totals 260 − 120 + 30 + 10 − 20 = 160 vs consolidated net income 200 (after tax), which needs unexplained corporate gains. The s5 rationale says 'external revenue must still be checked against the 75% test', but external revenue is not given separately.
fix: Show external and intersegment revenue in separate columns (with consolidated sales = external total), set the segment profit total above net income, and either remove the 75% remark or let candidates perform the test.

issue: The lesson never teaches going-concern evaluation or disclosure (ASC 205-40), yet four practice items in this module test it: the look-forward period (nd-12) and the disclosures required when management's plans alleviate substantial doubt (nd-13, nd-17, nd-24). No other lesson fills the gap: the only mention platform-wide is one sentence in the optional far-conceptual-framework lesson, and it gives the one-year period only. Nothing anywhere teaches the alleviated vs. not-alleviated disclosures, when management's plans may be considered, or the 'substantial doubt exists' statement.
evidence: grep -rl 'going concern|205-40' content/far/modules/*/lesson.md returns only far-conceptual-framework/lesson.md (line 167: one-year period only), and far.yaml marks that module optional: true. The lesson for this module has no going-concern heading, takeaway, or check. Items nd-12, 13, 17 and 24 are 4 of the 28 practice items (14%).
source: ASC 205-40-50-1 (one year after the date the statements are issued or available to be issued); 205-40-50-6 and 50-7 (management's plans are considered only if it is probable they will be effectively implemented and will mitigate the conditions); 205-40-50-12 (doubt alleviated: disclose the principal conditions, management's evaluation and the plans); 205-40-50-13 (doubt not alleviated: also state that there is substantial doubt)
fix: Add a 'Going concern (ASC 205-40)' section with: management's evaluation each annual and interim period; the look-forward window; the 'probable' threshold for substantial doubt; when plans count (probable implementation and mitigation); a two-column table of required disclosures, alleviated vs. not alleviated; a key takeaway; and an inline check. Add the ASC 205-40 citation to the frontmatter.

issue: Three practice items test interim financial reporting: the estimated-annual-effective-rate tax method (nd-25), allocation of an annual bonus across quarters (nd-26), and a temporary interim LIFO liquidation charged at replacement cost (nd-27). This module (notes, related parties, risk disclosures) does not teach any of it, and neither does any other FAR lesson. A learner who misses them is routed back to a lesson that cannot help. Whether the 2026 FAR Blueprint tests interim reporting at all (rather than BAR) is also unconfirmed.
evidence: grep -n interim content/far/modules/*/lesson.md finds only incidental mentions: far-inventory-valuation (interim write-down recoveries; gross-profit method for interim estimates), far-sec-segments (ASU 2023-07 interim segment disclosures) and far-income-statement-oci (DISE effective dates). No lesson covers the integral view, the ASC 740-270 effective-rate method, or ASC 270-10-45-6(b). Keys are right: nd-25 = 200,000 x 24% = 48,000 - 22,000 = 26,000; nd-26 = 120,000 / 4 = 30,000; nd-27 = replacement cost. One web search (query on the 2026 FAR blueprint and ASC 270) returned no primary or secondary source naming where interim reporting falls.
source: ASC 270-10-45-6(b), 270-10-45-8 to 45-10; ASC 740-270-30; AICPA 2026 FAR/BAR Blueprints (placement not verified)
fix: Confirm Blueprint placement. If interim reporting is FAR, add a short interim-reporting section to the module that owns it (for example far-income-statement-oci) and move nd-25 to nd-27 there (set moduleId). If it is BAR-only, mark the items optional: true or remove them. Either way, take them out of far-notes-disclosures.

issue: Two items test rules that this lesson does not teach and that sit in later modules. nd-14 tests ASC 440 unconditional purchase obligations, which are taught only in far-debt-other (unit u8) and far-contingencies (unit u12), both after this unit-u2 module. nd-28 tests the ASC 250-10-50-4 disclosure for a change in estimate (the effect on income from continuing operations, net income and per-share amounts). No lesson teaches that disclosure: far-accounting-changes covers disclosure only for changes in principle (line 70) and error corrections (line 98).
evidence: Module order in far.yaml puts far-notes-disclosures (u2) ahead of far-debt-other (u8) and far-contingencies (u12). grep -n 'unconditional purchase' finds far-contingencies/lesson.md:114 and far-debt-other/lesson.md:111 only. In far-accounting-changes/lesson.md the only disclosure lines are 70 (principle) and 98 (error).
fix: Move nd-14 to far-contingencies. Move nd-28 to far-accounting-changes and add the 250-10-50-4 disclosure sentence to that lesson. Alternatively, add a short 'Other required notes' section here (commitments, changes in estimate) before keeping the items in this module.

issue: These are single-fact recall items, yet each is labeled skill 'analysis' with difficulty 3 (nd-20: difficulty 2). Recall is 'remembering', so the skill label is two levels off, and the difficulty is inflated. The mislabel distorts the module's reported skill mix, which counts 13 analysis items among 30 MCQs when only about one MCQ (nd-08) is even arguably analysis.
evidence: nd-22 has the same stem as nd-11 ('Which item belongs in the summary of significant accounting policies?') and the same keyed concept (inventory cost method), yet nd-11 is labeled remembering/1 and nd-22 analysis/3. nd-20 is a yes/no recall of ASC 235-10-50-5. nd-17 and nd-24 restate ASC 205-40-50-12. nd-27 recalls ASC 270-10-45-6(b). nd-28 recalls ASC 250-10-50-4. nd-19 recalls ASC 850-10-50-6. None asks the candidate to examine relationships among data or documents, which is the Blueprint's definition of analysis.
source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints, skill-level definitions (Remembering & Understanding; Application; Analysis)
fix: Relabel all seven skill: remembering. Set difficulty 1 (nd-19 may be 2). Re-run the skill-mix tally: the module's MCQs are recall-heavy, and true analysis is covered only by the TBS (see the practice-design finding).

issue: Skill or difficulty is off by one level on these items. nd-08, nd-18, nd-21, nd-23, nd-25 and nd-26 each apply one rule to a short fact pattern or do one computation, which is application, but are labeled analysis. nd-13 is pure recall of ASC 205-40-50-12 but is labeled application/3, which is also inconsistent with its near-twins nd-17 and nd-24. Difficulty 3 is high for nd-21, nd-23 and nd-26 (nd-26 is 120,000 / 4).
evidence: nd-25: one step, 200,000 x 24% - 22,000 = 26,000. nd-26: 120,000 / 4 = 30,000. nd-23: the stem itself states that a severe impact is reasonably possible in the near term, so the candidate only matches the stated facts to the rule. nd-08 is the module's best item, but it still applies one rule (ASC 275-10-50-20) to facts; there is no multi-source analysis.
source: AICPA Blueprint skill definitions
fix: Relabel nd-08, nd-18, nd-21, nd-23, nd-25 and nd-26 as application. Relabel nd-13 as remembering. Set difficulty 2 for nd-21, nd-23, nd-26 and nd-13, and keep 3 for nd-08.

issue: nd-11 and nd-22 duplicate each other: identical stems, the same key concept (inventory cost method) and the same distractor types (debt maturities, composition of inventory or PP&E). The same 'policies note says how, not how much' fact is also tested by far-nd-pre1, far-nd-chk1 and far-nd-20. That is five classification items on one fact, all asked the same way.
evidence: cues.md Jaccard similarity nd-11 ~ nd-22 = 1.00. nd-11: key (d) 'The method used to cost inventory'. nd-22: key (b) 'The inventory cost method'.
fix: Replace nd-22 with an application item. For example, give five sentences from a draft Note 1 (including a debt-maturity table and an inventory composition breakdown) and ask which one must move to another note. Or delete nd-22.

issue: nd-13, nd-17 and nd-24 are near-identical: 'substantial doubt is alleviated by management's plans; what must be disclosed?', all keyed to the conditions and plans. Practicing one gives away the other two, and the not-alleviated case is never tested.
evidence: Stems: nd-13 'Conditions raise substantial doubt ... management concludes its plans alleviate the doubt. What must the notes disclose?'; nd-17 'Management concludes that its plans alleviate substantial doubt ... What disclosure is required?'; nd-24 'Substantial doubt ... exists but is alleviated by management's plans. What is required?' Keys: (b), (c) and (d), all 'conditions and plans'.
fix: Keep nd-13. Rewrite nd-17 to the not-alleviated case: the key adds an explicit statement that there is substantial doubt about the entity's ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the statements are issued. Rewrite nd-24 to test when management's plans may be considered: only when it is probable they will be effectively implemented and will mitigate the conditions.

issue: nd-19 has three problems. (1) The stem leaves out the condition that triggers the rule: the control relationship is disclosed only when it could make either entity's operating results or financial position significantly different from what they would be if the entities were autonomous. (2) Distractors (b) 'Nothing, absent transactions' and (d) 'Only if transactions occur' mean the same thing, so a candidate can eliminate both together, and the item becomes a 2-option guess between (a) and the implausible (c). (3) The trap label on (d), 'partial-computation', does not fit a non-numeric option.
evidence: Under ASC 850-10-50-6, (b) and (d) are both wrong for the same reason, and (d)'s explanation repeats (b)'s.
fix: Add to the stem: 'The common control could cause either company's results to differ significantly from those it would report if autonomous.' Replace (d) with a distinct misconception, such as 'Disclosure only in the parent's separate financial statements' (trap wrong-classification). Relabel the trap on (d).

issue: The lesson does not teach that a common-ownership or common-management control relationship must be disclosed even when there are no transactions between the entities (ASC 850-10-50-6). The flowchart even starts at 'Transaction with this party?', which implies that without a transaction nothing is disclosed. nd-19 tests this rule.
evidence: The related-parties section lists the four transaction disclosures and the exclusions only. The mermaid root node is 'Transaction with this party?'.
fix: Add a bullet: 'Control relationship: if the entity and others are under common ownership or management control, and the control could produce results significantly different from those of autonomous entities, disclose the nature of the control relationship even with no transactions.' Add a matching branch to the flowchart.

issue: The lesson's related-party definition and flashcard fc2 list 'management and their immediate families' but leave out the immediate families of principal owners. The ASC 850 glossary includes both. A learner could conclude that a 15% owner's spouse or child is not a related party.
evidence: Lesson: 'principal owners (more than 10% of voting interests), management and their immediate families'. fc2: 'principal owners (>10%), management & immediate family'. The ASC 850-10-20 definition of related parties includes 'members of the immediate families of principal owners of the entity and its management'.
source: ASC 850-10-20 (Related Parties; Immediate Family)
fix: Reword both as 'principal owners (>10%) and management, and members of the immediate families of either'.

issue: The special rule for labor and foreign-operation concentrations is stated imprecisely and incompletely. The lesson says to disclose 'the percentage covered and whether agreements expire within one year'. ASC 275 requires two percentages: the share of the labor force covered by collective bargaining agreements, and the share covered by agreements that will expire within one year. The required disclosure for operations outside the home country (carrying amounts of net assets and the geographic areas where they are located) is omitted. 'Are candidates' is also vague. The far-nd-18 explanation likewise never says what is disclosed.
evidence: Lesson text: 'Special rule: all concentrations of labor subject to collective bargaining agreements, and operations located outside the entity's home country, are candidates; for labor, disclose the percentage covered and whether agreements expire within one year when the vulnerability test is met.'
source: ASC 275-10-50-16 to 50-22 (labor subject to collective bargaining; operations outside the home country)
fix: Replace with: 'For labor under collective bargaining agreements, disclose the percentage of the labor force covered and the percentage covered by agreements expiring within one year. For operations outside the home country, disclose the carrying amounts of net assets and the geographic areas where they are located.'

issue: Explanations across the nd-17 to nd-28 block don't teach. Distractor explanations are circular ('Not the treatment.', 'Not the method.', 'Not the computation.', 'That isn't what the rule says.', 'That is not enough.', 'Not on these facts.'). Item-level explanations restate the key without the rule's authority or the computation.
evidence: nd-25 (c) $24,000: 'Not the computation.' The likely misconception (24% x an assumed $100,000 of Q2-only income) is never named. nd-26: the explanation never shows 120,000 / 4 = 30,000, even though calc is true. nd-27: no ASC 270-10-45-6(b) mechanics (COGS at expected replacement cost; the difference is carried as a current liability). nd-20 (c), (d): 'That isn't what the rule says.' nd-18: never states what is disclosed (the two percentages). None of nd-17 to nd-28 cites an ASC paragraph, while nd-03, 08, 12, 13 and 14 do.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 4
fix: Rewrite each distractor explanation to name the misconception and the rule. For example, nd-25 (c): '$24,000 applies 24% to an assumed $100,000 of Q2-only income; ASC 740-270 requires the cumulative YTD method: 48,000 - 22,000.' Add the computation and the ASC paragraph to each item-level explanation.

issue: Some trap labels don't match the misconception the distractor models.
evidence: nd-25 (b) $48,000 is YTD tax with Q1 not subtracted, but is labeled wrong-classification (it fits wrong-period or partial-computation). nd-25 (d) $22,000 is the Q1 amount, but is labeled reversed (it fits wrong-period). nd-20 (d) 'Only for inventory' is labeled partial-computation, though there is no computation. nd-20 (c) 'Only for public companies' is labeled wrong-classification (it fits wrong-rule). nd-19 (d) is labeled partial-computation for a non-numeric option.
source: src/content/schema.ts TRAP_TYPES
fix: Relabel: nd-25 (b) partial-computation; nd-25 (d) wrong-period; nd-20 (c) wrong-rule; nd-20 (d) overgeneralization; nd-19 (d) per the nd-19 rewrite.

issue: Weak distractors and a qualifier cue. nd-09: the key is the only hedged option ('preferably presented ...'), while every distractor makes an absolute claim. Distractor (c), 'optional if the statements include a statement of cash flows', is implausible. nd-20: (c) 'Only for public companies' and (d) 'Only for inventory' are implausible, which leaves (a) 'Yes, in full' versus (b) 'No'. nd-26: (c) '$120,000 in Q1' models no realistic misconception.
evidence: cues.md flags nd-09 (absolutes only in the distractors; key longest) and nd-20 (key much shortest). On inspection, nd-09 can be answered by spotting the only hedged option.
fix: nd-09 (c): use a plausible misconception, such as 'It must be repeated in unaudited interim statements even when policies are unchanged since year-end' (wrong per ASC 235-10-50-2), and give one distractor a hedge. nd-20: make it a judgment item, or replace (c) and (d) with plausible wrong answers ('Yes, the policies note must restate amounts so it can stand alone'). nd-26 (c): replace with '$40,000 a quarter for Q1-Q3' or 'Accrue only when the bonus becomes legally payable'.

issue: Answer cue: the stem asks which disclosure is 'most complete', and the key is the only option that lists everything: relationship, services, $250,000 and $40,000. It is also the longest option. A candidate can answer without knowing ASC 850.
evidence: cues.md: key longest; absolutes only in distractors b, c, d ('Only ...', 'No disclosure'). All three distractors open with 'Only' or 'No'.
fix: Ask 'Which disclosure meets ASC 850?' and write distractors of similar length that each look complete but have one defect. For example: one omits the $40,000 balance; one adds 'on terms equivalent to arm's length' without substantiation; one discloses the CEO's compensation instead of the fees.

issue: Answer cue in a mock-exam item. The key, 'Compensation arrangements and expense allowances in the ordinary course of business', is about twice as long as any distractor and quotes the ASC 850-10-50-1 exclusion verbatim. The distractors are short, concrete transactions, so the abstract, standards-worded option stands out.
evidence: Key length 82 characters vs. 47-52 for the distractors. cues.md: key much longest.
fix: Make the key a concrete transaction of similar length, e.g., 'The CFO's salary and annual bonus under the company's standard plan'.

issue: The explanation for distractor (d) says 'A loss is recognized only if the contract is onerous.' That is IFRS (IAS 37) language. U.S. GAAP has no general onerous-contract rule. A loss on a firm, noncancelable purchase commitment is recognized when the market price falls below the contract price. Stating it in IFRS terms misleads candidates on a U.S. GAAP exam.
evidence: IFRS has not been tested on the CPA Exam since the 2024 Blueprints (far-standards.md 1c). The platform's own far-contingencies lesson (line 36) states the U.S. GAAP rule: 'a loss is recognized on a firm, non-cancelable purchase commitment when the market price falls below the contract price'.
source: ASC 330-10-35-17 and 35-18 (losses on firm purchase commitments); ASC 440-10-50
fix: Change (d)'s explanation to: 'A loss is recognized only if the market price of the material falls below the contract price on a firm, noncancelable commitment (ASC 330-10-35-17); nothing in the stem indicates that.'

issue: The cash-paid-for-interest formula, 'interest expense - the increase in interest payable, ± premium or discount amortization', leaves the sign to the reader and ignores capitalized interest.
evidence: With a discount, cash paid = expense - discount amortization; with a premium, cash paid = expense + premium amortization. ASC 230 requires interest paid net of amounts capitalized.
fix: Write: 'cash paid for interest = interest expense - increase in interest payable - discount (and issue-cost) amortization + premium amortization; disclosed net of interest capitalized.'

issue: The intpd row assumes there is no discount, issue-cost amortization or capitalized interest, but the exhibit does not say so. The lesson's own formula includes those adjustments, so a careful candidate may hesitate. The 20-minute estimate is also generous for 11 straightforward tie-out rows.
evidence: Answer 58,000 = 64,000 - 6,000. This is correct only if no amortization or capitalization applies. Time estimate: 11 rows at roughly 1 minute each, plus reading the exhibits, is about 10 to 14 minutes.
fix: Add to the exhibit: 'No interest was capitalized, and the debt has no discount or issue costs.' Consider minutes: 15.

issue: The wording of the required related-party disclosures is slightly loose. The lesson and fc3 say 'the effects of any change in terms'; ASC 850 says 'the effects of any change in the method of establishing the terms from that used in the preceding period'. The ASC 850-10-50-1(d) requirement to disclose the terms and manner of settlement of balances (if not otherwise apparent) is omitted.
evidence: Lesson item 3: 'The dollar amounts of transactions and the effects of any change in terms'. fc3: 'Dollar amounts (and changes in terms)'.
fix: Reword item 3 as '... and the effects of any change in the method of establishing the terms', and add to item 4 '(and, if not otherwise apparent, the terms and manner of settlement)'. Mirror the change in fc3.

issue: The lesson has one pre-question (on the policies note) and two inline checks (policies note; supplier concentration). Nothing primes or checks related parties, which are the most-tested topic here (12 of 30 MCQs), or the tie-out skill behind the analysis objective and the TBS.
evidence: preQuestions: [far-nd-pre1]. Check blocks: far-nd-chk1 (policies) and far-nd-chk2 (concentration) only. The related-parties and 'Tying the notes' sections have no check.
source: Review brief section 3 (lesson design)
fix: Add a pre-question on arm's-length representations or principal owners, an inline check after the related-parties section (e.g., compensation vs. loan to an officer), and a numeric check after 'Tying the notes' (e.g., cash paid for interest).

issue: Practice-set design: no MCQ exercises the module's analysis objective (compare note disclosures with the statements and support). Only the TBS does. The nominally 'hard' end of the set (nd-17 to nd-28, all difficulty 3) is short recall, and only nd-08 is genuinely difficult, so the easy-to-hard progression is nominal. With corrected labels the MCQ mix is about 16 remembering, 13 application and 1 analysis, against the FAR Blueprint's 5-15% remembering, 45-55% application and 35-45% analysis allocation.
evidence: Objective 4 (analysis) has no MCQ. Relabelled skill counts come from the two skill-label findings above; the current labels show remembering 9, application 8 and analysis 13.
source: content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation; AICPA 2026 FAR Blueprint
fix: Add 3-4 application or analysis MCQs drawn from the tie-out section: cash paid for interest from expense and payable changes; whether a maturity table agrees to the current portion; depreciation vs. D&A; and spotting an unsubstantiated arm's-length claim in a draft note. Order practice items easy to hard.

issue: Readiness treats every module the diagnostic (or any single tutor/test answer) touched as "studied", so coverage jumps to ~100% and the unstudied-material penalty disappears. A learner who takes the dashboard's recommended diagnostic and then studies normally is told "Likely ready" (≈80) after one week with 26% of FAR lessons done. The code contradicts its own doc comment ("coverage: share of the area's modules studied (lesson done)").
evidence: scripts/learners.ts (FAR, 10 h/wk, real computeStudyState): 85% learner WITH diagnostic → end of week 1: lessons 26%, readiness 80 [76–84] "Likely ready"; the same learner WITHOUT the diagnostic → week 1: 52 "Early stage", week 3: 69 "Building", "Likely ready" only at week 4 with 91% of lessons. Cause: areaReadiness counts a module as studied when `lessonDone || status !== "not-started"`, and computeMastery sets status "learning" after any tutor/test attempt; buildDiagnostic samples ~1 item from nearly every module, so coverage ≈ 1 and estimate = accuracy on the few modules actually studied.
source: src/lib/analytics.ts areaReadiness (coverage), src/lib/mastery.ts computeMastery (status), src/lib/quiz.ts buildDiagnostic
fix: Compute coverage from lessonDone only (as documented), or from modules with ≥5 non-diagnostic practice answers; exclude diagnostic sessions (purpose "diagnostic") from mastery status. Better: estimate per module (studied → shrunken module accuracy; unstudied → 0.30) and weight modules within the area, so accuracy on 3 studied modules cannot stand in for 12. Add a regression test: diagnostic + 2 lessons must not raise readiness above the no-diagnostic value by more than the diagnostic evidence warrants.

issue: "Mastered" is reached by chance: two qualifying days (≥80% on ≥3 items) at any time ever, with failed mastery checks retried daily by the plan, so a learner whose true accuracy is 60% ends up with most modules "mastered". Qualifying days never expire, and a 3-item day needs 3/3 while a 5-item day needs 4/5 — tiny samples with no interval or prior.
evidence: Binomial: P(day qualifies | 5 own items, p) = 0.016 (p=.25), 0.337 (p=.60), 0.835 (p=.85); with daily retries P(two qualifying days within 10 checks) = 0.90 at p=.60. Wilson 95% lower bound of 4/5 is 0.38, of 3/3 is 0.44. Simulation (scripts/learners.ts, FAR 10 h/wk, fixed 60% accuracy incl. 10% of right answers marked Guess): 20–26 of 35 modules show "Mastered" by exam week; REG 60% learner 14–17/25.
source: src/lib/mastery.ts (MASTERY_THRESHOLD, MASTERY_DAYS, MIN_ITEMS_PER_DAY); src/lib/planner.ts buildQueue (re-adds checks daily)
fix: Base mastery on the module's recent delayed-retrieval record instead of best days: e.g. the last 10 distinct non-lesson items answered ≥1 day after the lesson, Wilson/Beta lower bound ≥0.65 (≈8/10 or 9/10), with the two most recent mastery checks both ≥80% and ≥5 own items each; expire qualifying days older than ~21 days. Space retries (see the planner finding) so a pass cannot come from repetition of the same items on consecutive days.

issue: Failed mastery checks are re-added every day with no spacing and no remediation step, and because the queue is ordered unit by unit, all of them are scheduled before any lesson of a later unit. A struggling learner's plan becomes the same failing checks every day and new material stops; the status line still says "On track" because the plan assumes each check passes first time.
evidence: scripts/learners.ts (FAR, 10 h/wk, exam in 12 wk): random guesser — day 28 and day 56 plans are "8 mastery checks, 0 lesson tasks"; lessons stop at 26% from week 2 to the exam; day-28 status "On track: new material finishes by 2026-12-12". 60% learner at 5 h/wk reaches only 74% of FAR lessons by exam day (85% learner: 100%). REG guesser: lessons stop at 32%.
source: src/lib/planner.ts buildQueue / readyOn (a mastery item with no `after` and no lastMasteryDay is ready immediately)
fix: Track the last mastery-check attempt per module (pass or fail) and pass it to the planner: after a failed check, schedule a remediation task (rework faded example + flashcards) and set notBefore = last attempt + 2 days for the retry. Cap mastery retries per day (e.g. 2) and never let retries of earlier units block first-pass lessons when the projected finish is after the final-review start. Count expected retries in requiredMinutes so the status is honest.

issue: With no data at all, the adaptive unit order (area weight × default weakness 0.5) reorders AUD and REG for a new learner: AUD starts with Area III evidence, sampling and substantive procedures before ethics, planning, materiality, risk assessment and internal control; REG starts with C corporations and flow-through entities before individual taxation and property basis (REG-III comes last). There is no prerequisite metadata in the schema, so the reorder cannot respect dependencies, and lessons then rely on concepts taught later.
evidence: scripts/planner.ts: AUD new-learner unit order aud-u6 → u7 → u8 → u3 → u9 → u4 → u5 → u1 → u2 → u10; REG reg-u6 → u7 → u4 → u5 → u2 → u1 → u3 (FAR and TCP keep course order only because area weights tie). Day-1 next action: AUD "Lesson: Sufficient appropriate evidence & assertions"; REG "Lesson: C corporation taxable income". Dependencies: aud-sampling lesson uses tolerable misstatement and risk of overreliance (taught in aud-risk-materiality u3, aud-tests-of-controls u5); reg-partnerships uses outside basis, §1231 and §179; reg-c-corp-income uses capital-loss and cost-recovery rules (reg-capital-gains, reg-cost-recovery, both u3).
source: src/lib/studyState.ts unitPriority (weakness 0.5 when no estimate); src/lib/planner.ts orderUnits; src/content/schema.ts ModuleRef (no prerequisites field)
fix: Apply priority ordering only after a diagnostic or ≥5 answers per area, and only among units whose prerequisites are done. Add `prerequisites: [unitId|moduleId]` to UnitConfig/ModuleRef (e.g. aud-u6 after aud-u3, aud-u5; reg-u6/u7 after reg-u3, reg-u4) and topologically sort with priority as the tie-breaker. Until then, keep course order for untouched units.

issue: Every mock form tests far less Analysis than the Blueprint: the exam-pool MCQs are almost all Remembering/Application, so a form's score-weighted skill mix misses the Analysis range in all four sections. The validator only checks the pooled practice+exam+TBS mix, so it passes.
evidence: scripts/forms.ts, score-weighted (MCQ share × 50% + TBS share × 50%) Remembering/Application/Analysis/Evaluation: FAR forms 6/78/16/0, 9/78/13/0, 10/80/10/0 vs Blueprint R 5–15, Ap 45–55, An 35–45; REG 16/84/0/0, 19/74/6/0, 15/78/6/0 vs R 25–35, Ap 35–45, An 25–35; TCP 10/90/0/0, 10/75/14/0, 14/86/0/0 vs R 5–15, Ap 55–65, An 25–35; AUD 23/54/16/8, 26/45/8/21, 23/47/8/22 vs R 30–40, Ap 30–40, An 15–25, Ev 5–15. Exam-pool MCQ Analysis share: FAR 8.7%, AUD 1.3%, REG 0%, TCP 0% (practice pools 41%, 22%, 40%, 31%).
source: content/sections/*.yaml skillAllocation; src/content/build.ts skill-mix warning (pooled)
fix: Write analysis-level exam MCQs (multi-step computations, interpreting exhibits) so each form's weighted mix lands in range — e.g. FAR ≈ 15 of 50 MCQs at Analysis plus 3 Analysis TBS; REG/TCP ≈ 15–20 Analysis MCQs per form; AUD ≈ 10. Add a per-form validator check (score-weighted, ±5 points) next to the per-area check in tests/mockForms.test.ts.

issue: Mock MCQs are much easier than the practice bank (by the content's own difficulty tags), and the forms are static. The real exam's second MCQ testlet is medium or difficult depending on performance on the first. Scored with the 65% → 75 rule of thumb, the mocks overstate readiness, and readiness blends the latest mock 50/50.
evidence: scripts/stats.ts / forms.ts — difficulty 1/2/3 in exam pools: FAR 22/72/10 (10% hard), AUD 77/75/4 (3%), REG 52/96/0 (0%), TCP 33/77/26 (19%); practice pools are 45%, 32%, 40%, 44% hard. Per form: reg-mock-1/2/3 have 0 hard MCQs; aud-mock-2 has 1 of 78; far-mock-3 has 3 of 50.
source: AICPA, CPA Exam scoring (multistage testing: testlet 1 medium, testlet 2 medium or difficult); src/lib/analytics.ts approxScaledScore
fix: Rebalance each form to a realistic mix (e.g. testlet 1 ≈ 25/50/25 easy/medium/hard, testlet 2 ≈ 10/45/45) and/or make testlet 2 adaptive (pick a harder testlet when testlet-1 ≥ 60%). Until then, show the form's difficulty mix on the results page and weight raw items by difficulty before the scaled-score mapping, or raise the pass anchor for these forms.

issue: Forms 2 and 3 each reuse half of form 1's MCQs, but nothing tells the learner, and the results page says mock items stay out of review "so later mocks stay fresh". After reviewing form 1's explanations, a learner's form-2 score is inflated, and readiness uses the latest mock.
evidence: scripts/forms.ts: shared with form 1 — FAR 25/50 on each later form, AUD 39/78, REG 36/72, TCP 34/68. Illustration: true accuracy 65% on new items and 90% on reviewed items → form-2 MCQ 77.5% instead of 65%; with TBS at 65% the weighted score rises 65% → 71.25% and approxScaledScore 75 → 79; readiness (50% mock blend) moves ~+2–3 scaled points from recognition alone.
source: src/pages/ExamPlayer.tsx ExamResults ("kept out of spaced review so later mocks stay fresh"); src/lib/studyState.ts lastMock blend
fix: Either build forms 2–3 from fresh items (≈50 more FAR exam MCQs, 78 AUD, 72 REG, 68 TCP), or mark reused items, report a "fresh items only" score next to the total, and blend only fresh-item performance into readiness. On ExamHome, say which forms overlap and recommend taking form 1 last if only one is used for readiness.

issue: The simulations on each form are budgeted (their own `minutes`) for more time than the 4-hour clock leaves after the MCQs at the app's 90-second pace, so the pacing targets on the results page add up to more than 240 minutes and a candidate who follows them runs out of time.
evidence: scripts/forms.ts: suggested TBS minutes vs time left after MCQs at 90 s — REG 195/200/180 vs 132 (72 MCQs = 108 min; total 303–308 min); TCP 190/180/180 vs 138; AUD 150/150/145 vs 123; FAR 180/160/170 vs 165. Real-exam arithmetic for REG: 132 min ÷ 8 TBS ≈ 16.5 min per TBS.
source: src/lib/pacing.ts MCQ_TARGET_MS; src/pages/ExamPlayer.tsx pacing targets
fix: Calibrate exam-pool TBS `minutes` so each form fits (e.g. REG ≈ 16 min, TCP/AUD ≈ 18–20, FAR ≈ 23), trimming parts where a TBS is genuinely longer than a real one; compute the results-page targets as the clock share actually available (remaining time ÷ TBS count) and add a validator check that MCQ×1.5 + Σ TBS minutes ≤ durationMinutes.

issue: Mock results do not reach the weak-area tools. The results page ends with "open Analytics for your full weak-area breakdown", but Analytics, the recommendations and the planner's unit priority all use scoringAttempts(), which drops mock (mode "exam") attempts. The only routes from a mock miss back to study are the opt-in "add missed questions to spaced review" button and the per-item error tagger.
evidence: src/lib/analytics.ts scoringAttempts filters a.mode !== "exam"; src/pages/Analytics.tsx byArea/bySkill use scoringAttempts; src/lib/studyState.ts weakestModules stats use scoringAttempts and unitPriority uses practice-only area estimates; ExamResults has no per-area or per-module links.
source: src/pages/ExamPlayer.tsx; src/pages/Analytics.tsx; src/lib/studyState.ts
fix: Add a "Latest mock" panel to Analytics (by area and by module, MCQ and TBS), feed mock misses into weakestModules with their own reason ("Missed 4 of 6 on the mock"), and on ExamResults link each area to its weakest modules and each missed item to its lesson.

issue: A correct answer marked "Unsure" is graded Hard. In ts-fsrs 5 a Hard rating during the learning steps repeats the current step (~6 minutes) instead of advancing, so a question a learner keeps answering correctly but "Unsure" never graduates: it is due again minutes later after every review, forever, rather than being spaced. Flashcards rated Hard behave the same way while learning.
evidence: scripts/srs.ts (app parameters: retention 0.9, max 365 d, learning steps 1m/10m, fuzz off): missed, then unsure-correct ×6 → 1m, 6m, 6m, 6m, 6m, 6m, 6m — still in learning, stability 0.2 d, predicted recall on day 56 = 0.42. Missed, then confident ×6 → 1m, 10m, 1d, 2d, 7d, 19d, 48d.
source: ts-fsrs 5.4.2 basic scheduler (Hard on a learning step = same step); src/lib/srs.ts gradeFromAttempt
fix: Grade unsure-correct as Good while the card is New/Learning/Relearning and as Hard only in the Review state (or map Unsure → Good and use the reduced stability via a lower desired retention for that item). Add a test that an unsure-correct path graduates to a ≥1-day interval within 3 answers.

issue: Questions share the flashcard learning steps (1 m, 10 m). A missed question is "due" one minute later, so the dashboard immediately says "Review N due items" and the learner re-answers it minutes after reading its explanation; those near-immediate correct answers count as successful reviews and advance the schedule. True spacing starts only on the third answer.
evidence: scripts/srs.ts: missed → due in 1m → answered confidently → 10m → 1d → 2d → 7d … (the first two "reviews" happen within the same session). src/db/actions.ts scheduleQuestion schedules every missed/guessed/unsure practice answer, including lesson pre-questions answered before the lesson is read.
source: src/lib/srs.ts (generatorParameters defaults: learning_steps ["1m","10m"]); src/db/actions.ts scheduleQuestion
fix: Use a separate FSRS instance for questions with learning_steps ["1d"] (or enable_short_term false) so the first re-ask is the next day; skip scheduling lesson pre-questions (or schedule them for the day after the lesson is completed).

issue: The scheduler ignores the exam date: retention 0.9 and a 365-day maximum interval apply throughout, and nothing in the final-review window targets items whose predicted recall on exam day is low. Overshooting the exam is not itself harmful (an item due after the exam is still ≥0.90 on exam day under the model), but 0.90 per item is a modest target for the last two weeks.
evidence: scripts/srs.ts: a missed item answered confidently each time it is due reaches predicted recall 0.904 (exam in 28 d), 0.935 (56 d), 0.991 (84 d) on exam day, with the next due date after the exam. A lapsed item reviewed 3 more times is at 0.67 on day 56 only if not reviewed again — i.e. the model relies on the learner doing every due review.
source: src/lib/srs.ts generatorParameters; src/lib/planner.ts reviewMinutes
fix: In the final-review window, raise request_retention for question cards to ~0.95 or add a "pre-exam sweep" task listing items with predicted recall on exam day < 0.95 (ts-fsrs get_retrievability at the exam date); cap maximum_interval at days-to-exam.

issue: The readiness label is taken from the point estimate (≥75 → "Likely ready") even when the plausible range dips well below 75, and the range itself is only the binomial error of first-attempt accuracy: it ignores the 0.30 assumption for unstudied material, the area weighting and, above all, the raw-to-scaled mapping, which the mock page itself calls a rule of thumb. The dashboard shows "≈ 80 Likely ready, likely range 76–84" with no caveat.
evidence: overallReadiness: se = sqrt(p(1−p)/n), band = approxScaledScore(raw ± 1.96 se), label from `overall` only. Simulation: 85% learner band 79–87 (±4 scaled) from 180 first attempts; at n=200, raw 0.66 → overall 76 "Likely ready" with band 69–81. The IRT caveat appears only on ExamResults.
source: src/lib/analytics.ts overallReadiness / approxScaledScore; src/pages/Dashboard.tsx
fix: Label from the lower bound ("Likely ready" only if band[0] ≥ 75; "Borderline" if the band straddles 75), add a fixed mapping-uncertainty term (e.g. ±5 scaled) to the band, and repeat the one-line caveat under the dashboard readiness number.

issue: Readiness treats confidence labels inconsistently, so honest labelling lowers it: a correct answer marked "Guess" counts as wrong, while unlabelled test-mode answers and mock answers count in full. Two learners with identical knowledge get very different readiness depending on how honestly they click.
evidence: scripts/learners.ts, FAR 10 h/wk: random guesser who marks every answer "Guess" sees readiness 12–18 (with diagnostic) or 28–30; the same guesser clicking "Confident" sees 29–38. QuizPlayer finishTest passes confidence undefined when not given, and isTrulyCorrect counts that as known.
source: src/lib/mastery.ts isTrulyCorrect; src/lib/analytics.ts rate(strict); src/pages/QuizPlayer.tsx finishTest
fix: Keep "guess = miss" for mastery and spaced review, but for the readiness estimate (a prediction of exam score, where lucky guesses do score) count answers as answered, or use calibrated credit (correct guesses at the learner's own guess accuracy). Make the treatment of unlabelled answers explicit and identical across modes.

issue: Readiness disappears for long stretches: the whole estimate is withheld whenever any area has some coverage but fewer than 5 first attempts. The 40-item diagnostic gives small areas fewer than 5 items, and finishing the first lesson of a new area before its practice set also nulls the estimate.
evidence: scripts/learners.ts REG (10 h/wk): after the diagnostic REG-III has 4 items, so readiness reads "Not enough data yet" until week 8 for the 60% learner, week 4 for the 85% learner and for all 12 weeks for both random guessers, despite 89–300 first attempts. FAR 60% learner at 5 h/wk: readiness shown at week 4, then "Not enough data yet" again at week 8 (Area II n<5 after its first lesson). The message "Answer at least 15 new practice questions" is wrong in these cases.
source: src/lib/analytics.ts areaReadiness (estimate null when n<5 and coverage>0), overallReadiness (null if any area null); src/lib/quiz.ts buildDiagnostic quota rounding
fix: Never null the whole estimate for one thin area: shrink the area's accuracy toward a prior (e.g. Beta(3,7) ≈ 0.30) and widen the band instead. Give every area at least 5 diagnostic items. Make the "not enough data" message name the area that is short.

issue: Readiness evidence is the last 60 first attempts per area, which are mostly blocked practice answered minutes after reading the lesson. Retention is never measured: answers to already-seen items days or weeks later (mixed sets, mastery checks, the review queue) are excluded by design, and older modules drop out of the 60-item window.
evidence: firstAttempts keeps only each item's first sighting; areaReadiness slices the last 60 per area. FAR Area I has 12 in-scope modules × 10-item practice sets, so the window spans only the last ~6 modules studied; the estimate never reflects forgetting of the first ones.
source: src/lib/analytics.ts firstAttempts / areaReadiness
fix: Weight first attempts by delay since the module's lesson (e.g. only items first seen ≥3 days after the lesson count fully), or add a retention term from mixed-set accuracy on items last seen ≥7 days earlier; sample the window per module rather than per area.

issue: "Slipping" is triggered by a single day with ≥3 items under 60%, so mastered status flickers for strong learners.
evidence: scripts/learners.ts FAR 85% learner: mastered modules by week 5–12 = 33, 32, 34, 28, 32, 35, 31, 30 of 35 with constant true accuracy. P(≤1 of 3 correct | p=.85) = 0.061 per 3-item day.
source: src/lib/mastery.ts (last.acc < 0.6)
fix: Mark slipping only when the last ≥8 mixed answers for the module (across days) fall below ~65%, or when two consecutive qualifying-size days fail.

issue: The planner's model of the work is a small fraction of what passing takes, so it reports "On track" for plans that cannot prepare a candidate. Required work counts each lesson, one 10-question set, two 10-minute mastery checks, 15 minutes per practice TBS and one mock — about 33–46 hours per section — against the 300–400 hours a working adult needs, and even against the ~84–92 hours one pass through the app's own content takes.
evidence: scripts/planner.ts: planner's whole-course model FAR 46.0 h, AUD 43.6 h, REG 36.9 h, TCP 32.7 h (new-learning portion 42.0 / 39.6 / 32.9 / 28.7 h). One pass through the app content (lessons + all practice MCQs at 2.5 min incl. explanation + practice TBS at 1.5× suggested minutes + 3 mocks + 3 reviews): FAR 91.5 h, AUD 86.1 h, REG 83.5 h, TCP 85.5 h. "FAR exam in 12 wk, 5 h/wk" (60 h in total) → "On track: new material finishes by 2026-12-24". The plan budgets 15 min per TBS while practice TBS average 19–22 suggested minutes. At 5 h/wk the plan leaves 0.3–3 h for mixed practice, so 60–70% of each module's bank is never scheduled.
source: src/lib/planner.ts PRACTICE_MINUTES, MASTERY_MINUTES, TBS_MINUTES, buildQueue; docs (300–400 h per section is the brief's assumption and common review-course guidance)
fix: Give each section a target-hours figure (data in the section YAML, e.g. FAR 350, AUD 300, REG 300, TCP 250) and show "Your plan provides X of ~Y recommended hours" whenever weekly hours × weeks falls short; schedule the whole practice bank (all MCQs in sets of ~15, every practice TBS at its own minutes, three mocks plus 2-hour reviews) so requiredMinutes reflects real work.

issue: Mock-exam scheduling is thin: only one mock is planned although three forms exist, there is no review block after it, it always sits on the first day of the final-review window, and it is still scheduled when most of the syllabus is unstudied.
evidence: scripts/planner.ts: every dated scenario has exactly one 4-hour mock and none after mockTaken; "FAR exam in 4 wk, 5 h/wk": 21 of 35 lessons never scheduled but the mock is on day 23; "FAR exam in 4 days": lessons on day 1 and a 4-hour mock on day 2.
source: src/lib/planner.ts generatePlan (mockDay)
fix: Plan form 1 about 3–4 weeks out (diagnostic of exam conditions), forms 2–3 in the final window, each followed by a 2-hour "review the mock" task; skip the mock (and say why) when the projected lesson coverage at that date is below ~70% or the exam is under a week away.

issue: Each section is planned in isolation for the active section and assumes the learner's entire weekly budget, so a candidate with two exam dates (e.g. FAR in 6 weeks, AUD in 14) gets two plans that each consume all of their hours, and the AUD plan is invisible while FAR is active.
evidence: scripts/planner.ts [multi-section]: FAR (exam +6 wk) plan week 1 = 9.8 h; AUD (exam +14 wk) plan week 1 = 9.8 h; weekly budget = 10 h.
source: src/lib/studyState.ts (generatePlan called with settings.minutesByWeekday for the active section only)
fix: Allocate the weekly budget across sections with upcoming dates (e.g. all to the nearest exam until it passes, or a user-set split), and show the next section's start date on the planner.

issue: FAR's course order follows the Blueprint areas, so Area I lessons that depend on later material come first: EPS (if-converted bonds, treasury stock method) in unit 2, consolidations (equity method, goodwill) in unit 3, the cash flow statement (finance leases, deferred tax, impairment) and OCI (AFS securities) in unit 1 — while bonds, equity investments, intangibles, leases and income taxes are taught in units 6–11.
evidence: grep of lesson bodies: far-eps mentions if-converted ×3, treasury stock method ×3, convertible bonds ×2 (taught in far-bonds/far-equity, unit 8); far-consolidations: equity method, goodwill ×4 (far-equity-investments unit 7, far-intangibles unit 6); far-cash-flows: finance lease, deferred tax expense, impairment, patent amortization; far-income-statement-oci: available-for-sale, fair value option.
source: content/sections/far.yaml module order; content/far/modules/*/lesson.md
fix: Reorder the course (not the Blueprint mapping): statements basics → Area II accounts → Area III transactions → consolidations, EPS, cash flows, ratios as capstones; or add prerequisite metadata and a one-paragraph primer in each early lesson. Per-module reviewers should confirm how much each lesson actually assumes.

issue: Item difficulty is authored on every MCQ but never used: practice sets, mastery checks, mixed sets and the diagnostic ignore it, so there is no easy→hard progression. The first practice set right after a 15–20 minute lesson is a random draw from a bank that is up to 45% "hard".
evidence: grep: `difficulty` appears nowhere in src/ outside the schema. Practice difficulty 1/2/3: FAR 17/38/45%, AUD 27/40/32%, REG 23/37/40%, TCP 13/43/44%; five FAR modules are >50% hard (e.g. far-leases-operating 3/7/18). Authored file order is roughly easy→hard in only 11/37 FAR, 3/33 AUD, 4/27 REG, 2/19 TCP modules (scripts/practice.ts).
source: src/lib/quiz.ts buildQuiz / buildMasteryCheck; content/*/modules/*/questions.json
fix: For the first blocked set after a lesson, draw ~4 easy, 4 medium, 2 hard in that order; for mastery checks draw medium/hard; for repeat sets prefer the difficulty band where the learner's accuracy is 60–85%.

issue: Skill-mix checks are pooled and lenient: the validator mixes practice MCQs, exam MCQs and TBS into one share per section, does not weight by score, and does not flag a skill level the section's Blueprint does not use. Pool-level gaps remain: FAR practice Application 43.9% (Blueprint 45–55%); REG practice Application 34.3% (35–45%) and Analysis 40.0% (25–35%); two TBS are tagged Evaluation in sections with no Evaluation level.
evidence: scripts/stats.ts: FAR practice R/Ap/An 14.7/43.9/41.4%; REG 25.7/34.3/40.0%; TCP 13.0/55.8/31.3%; AUD 31.1/37.3/21.5/10.1%. scripts/misc.ts: reg-tbs-r3-circular230 and tcp-tbs-r3-planning have skill "evaluation" (REG/TCP skillAllocation has no evaluation entry). The validator prints 0 warnings.
source: src/content/build.ts (skill mix warning); content/sections/reg.yaml, tcp.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Check each pool separately and each mock form score-weighted; error on a skill level outside the section's allocation; relabel the two TBS (Analysis) and re-tag or add REG Application items.

issue: The per-area check (tests/mockForms.test.ts) counts MCQs only. Counting the TBS half of the score, REG-III is over-weighted on every REG form, REG-V is under on reg-mock-3, and AUD-IV is over on every AUD form.
evidence: scripts/forms.ts, score-weighted area share (50% MCQ + 50% TBS by the TBS's first module): REG-III 17%, 17%, 24% vs Blueprint 5–15% (2–3 of 8 TBS are property transactions); REG-V on reg-mock-3 20% vs 23–33%; AUD-IV 22%, 22%, 22% vs 10–20% (2 of 7 TBS). FAR and TCP forms are within range.
source: tests/mockForms.test.ts (MCQ-only area check); content/sections/reg.yaml, aud.yaml allocations
fix: Extend the area test to the score-weighted mix (±5 points) and swap one REG-III TBS for an REG-V entity TBS on each REG form and one AUD-IV TBS for an AUD-II/III TBS.

issue: Four mock items are near-clones of practice items the learner will already have answered, which contaminates those forms.
evidence: scripts/misc.ts: far-x1-29 (far-mock-3) asks the same discontinued-operations question as far-iso-02 with the same key; reg-x2-24 (reg-mock-3) = reg-ag-14 ("Which duty does a principal owe an agent?"); tcp-x4-08 (reg-mock-1, reg-mock-3) has the same stem, numbers ($4,600,000 placed in service) and answer ($1,900,000) as practice item reg-dep-04; tcp-x1-17 (tcp-mock-1, tcp-mock-2) = tcp-re-01 with the age changed from 52 to 62.
source: content/far/exam-questions/far-exam-area1.json etc.
fix: Rewrite the four exam items to test the same rule with a different scenario or different numbers (or replace them), and add a validator check for exam-pool stems that match a practice or lesson stem.

issue: Misses do not route back to the specific lesson. After an answer is revealed (practice, review queue, mixed sets, mock review), the learner gets the explanation and an error-cause tagger, but no link to the module's lesson or the relevant worked example, and in mixed and review sets the module is not even named. The error-log advice for "Concept gap" says "Re-read the lesson's big idea" without saying which lesson.
evidence: src/components/McqView.tsx (revealed branch: explanation, ErrorTagger, report link only); src/pages/QuizPlayer.tsx QuizResults list has no module links; only the failed-mastery Remediation panel and Analytics' recent tagged misses link to /module/:id.
source: src/components/McqView.tsx; src/pages/QuizPlayer.tsx; src/pages/ExamPlayer.tsx
fix: After reveal, show "Review: <module title> → lesson" (deep-link to the heading or worked block that teaches the item, via an optional `lessonAnchor` on the MCQ); on results pages group misses by module with a "Review lesson" button.

issue: The dashboard's main "next step" can be hijacked: any lesson that has been opened but not completed becomes "Continue lesson" ahead of the plan, indefinitely, even if the learner only glanced at an upcoming or optional module. The fallback "Study next" uses course order rather than the plan's (reordered) order.
evidence: computeStudyState: inLesson = latest progress with lastVisitedAt and no lessonCompletedAt; ModulePage calls touchModule on every visit; `next` checks inLesson before the plan's first task. Fallback: available.find(m => !m.lessonDone) (course order).
source: src/lib/studyState.ts; src/pages/ModulePage.tsx touchModule
fix: Use "Continue lesson" only when the lesson was scrolled past ~10% within the last few days and is in scope; otherwise show it in the secondary "Where you left off" line. Make the fallback follow orderUnits.

issue: The REG final-review docs leave out most of REG-I and REG-II (25–45% of the exam): nothing on Circular 230 duties beyond return-position standards and penalty thresholds, accountants' legal liability, agency, contract formation and remedies beyond the statute of frauds and mailbox rule, business structures, federal regulation (ACA employer rules, worker classification, FCPA) or state and local tax. There is no REG high-yield summary at all, and the "Computation roadmap" spends much of its space on topics REG marks optional (like-kind, §1245/§1250/§291, installment sales, E&P, §351, redemption attribution).
evidence: grep across content/reg/review/*.md: no match for "Circular 230|§10.", "liab|privity|10b-5", "agency|agent", "nexus|apportion", "FCPA|ACA|worker". Docs: reg-exam-day (orientation), reg-formulas (condensed), reg-mnemonics, reg-numbers. FAR and AUD each have an area-by-area high-yield doc.
source: content/sections/reg.yaml (REG-I 10–20%, REG-II 15–25%); docs/BLUEPRINT_NOTES.md decision D1
fix: Add reg-high-yield.md organised by Blueprint area (ethics and procedures, business law, property, individuals, entities, SALT) and mark or move the TCP-scope rows in reg-formulas.md (e.g. "TCP — optional in REG").

issue: TCP has no high-yield summary, and its review docs do not cover international tax (a whole module), consolidated returns or choice of entity (Area III).
evidence: grep across content/tcp/review/*.md: no match for "international|CFC|GILTI|FDAP|foreign tax credit", "consolidated", "entity choice|choice of entity".
source: content/sections/tcp.yaml (TCP-III 10–20%)
fix: Add tcp-high-yield.md by Blueprint area, including an entity-choice comparison table, consolidated-return basics and the international rules taught in tcp-international.

issue: FAR and AUD final-review docs are solid but skip a few Blueprint topics: FAR special purpose frameworks and related-party disclosures; AUD data analytics, GAGAS/single audits and SSAE examination specifics beyond one line.
evidence: grep across content/far/review/*.md: no match for "special purpose|cash basis", "related part"; content/aud/review/*.md: no match for "data analytic|ADA", "single audit|GAGAS|Yellow".
source: content/sections/far.yaml, aud.yaml

issue: Lesson depth is modest for a 300–400 hour target: each module is one ~800–1,000-word lesson, so the whole section reads in 6–10 hours, and the app's content supports roughly 85–92 hours of study per section. The `minutes` values are realistic (if anything generous); the issue is total depth, which the app should state if it is meant as a companion to a full course.
evidence: scripts/lessons.ts: stated vs estimated reading time (130 wpm + 1.5 min per embedded/pre question + 2 min per faded example): FAR 636 vs 524 min, AUD 529 vs 354, REG 474 vs 313, TCP 369 vs 239; mean words per lesson 1,019 / 794 / 847 / 828. One-pass hours from scripts/planner.ts: 91.5 / 86.1 / 83.5 / 85.5.
source: content/*/modules/*/lesson.md
fix: Either say plainly (README, onboarding, planner) that the app covers roughly a quarter of recommended study time and works best alongside a full review course, or deepen the highest-weight modules (multiple lessons per module for revenue, leases, consolidations, risk assessment, individual and entity tax).

issue: The worked → faded → independent sequence promised in PLAN.md is missing in most AUD and REG lessons (no faded example), including computational REG modules.
evidence: scripts/lessons.ts: lessons with no faded block — AUD 30/33, REG 19/27, FAR 3/37, TCP 2/19.
source: PLAN.md "Worked → faded → independent"

issue: The set-complete message says "N question(s) were added to your spaced review queue" counting only misses and lucky guesses; correct-but-unsure answers are also queued, and in review mode items are rescheduled rather than added.
evidence: QuizResults: `missed + guessedRight` vs src/lib/srs.ts needsRequeue (also true for unsure).
source: src/pages/QuizPlayer.tsx

issue: Contradiction: aud-ss-26 keys the superseded pre-SSARS 25 rule ('Disclose it in a paragraph'; explanation: departures are disclosed in a separate paragraph of the review report), and its option (b) feedback implies a review can't be adverse. aud-ss-07 in the same module correctly keys a qualified or adverse review conclusion.
evidence: SSARS No. 25 (effective for reviews of periods ending on or after Dec 15, 2021) replaced the 'disclose the departure in a separate paragraph' review report with modified conclusions: qualified when the misstatement is material, adverse when it is material and pervasive, each with a 'Basis for Qualified (Adverse) Conclusion' section. aud-ss-07's own explanation states this. A student who answers aud-ss-26 using aud-ss-07's rule finds no option for it and is told the old rule is correct.
source: SSARS No. 25; AR-C 90 (modified conclusions)
fix: Change aud-ss-26 option (d) to 'Modify the conclusion: qualified, or adverse if the effects are pervasive' and keep it as the key. Rewrite the explanation to match aud-ss-07. Make option (b) 'Issue an adverse audit opinion' with the feedback 'A review expresses a conclusion, not an opinion'.

issue: Contradiction on year-specific due dates. Exam items reg-x5-41 (2025 Form 1065 keyed 'March 15, 2026') and reg-x5-44 (2025 S election keyed 'March 15, 2025') ignore the weekend rule. tcp-po-06 keys March 16, 2026, tcp-sc2-01 keys March 17, 2025, and the platform's own TBS (reg-tbs-x5-research, tcp-tbs-u4-k1) and content/tcp/review/tcp-numbers.md use March 16, 2026.
evidence: Python datetime: March 15, 2026 is a Sunday and March 15, 2025 is a Saturday. Under IRC §7503 the deadline moves to the next business day: Monday March 16, 2026 and Monday March 17, 2025. A student drilled on tcp-po-06 or reg-tbs-x5-research would look for March 16 and find it missing. The keyed option is the only defensible one among the choices, so the key isn't wrong, but the stated date is not the actual deadline.
fix: reg-x5-41: change option (c) to 'March 16, 2026 (March 15 is a Sunday)' and add §7503 to the explanation. reg-x5-44: change option (b) to 'March 17, 2025 (March 15 is a Saturday)' with the same note. Or drop the year from both stems and answers, as reg-pt-08 and reg-sc-16 do.

issue: Contradiction: aud-qm-13 keys 'Listed-entity audits and others required' as the SQMS No. 1 engagement-quality-review requirement. aud-qm-23 keys 'Those the firm designates' plus those required by law or regulation. The module lesson (SQMS No. 2 section) also omits any listed-entity trigger. The listed-entity requirement comes from IAASB ISQM 1, not the AICPA standard.
evidence: AICPA SQMS No. 1 (QM 10.34f) requires EQRs for (i) engagements where law or regulation requires one and (ii) engagements the firm determines need one in response to assessed quality risks. Unlike ISQM 1, it has no listed-entity criterion (issuer audits get EQRs under PCAOB AS 1220). The lesson says: 'Required for engagements the firm's policies specify ... and where required by law or regulation.'
source: SQMS No. 1 (QM 10.34f); SQMS No. 2 (QM 20); ISQM 1 para 34(f) for comparison
fix: Reword aud-qm-13 option (c) to 'Those required by law or regulation and those the firm determines need one to address quality risks'. Remove 'audits of listed entities' from the explanation, or note it as the IAASB ISQM 1 rule, and align it with aud-qm-23 and the lesson.

issue: Some distractor rationales misstate the arithmetic that produces the distractor, or describe an incoherent error.
evidence: 01(d) 64,000 is explained as weighting the issuance 4 months and the treasury purchase 8 months. That reversal gives 60,000 + 12,000x4/12 - 6,000x8/12 = 60,000, not 64,000. 64,000 = 60,000 + 8,000 - 6,000x8/12, i.e. the treasury shares weighted 8 months. 02(c) 50,833 = 50,000 + 5,000x2/12. Time-weighting a dividend distributed March 1 of the following year would add 0 shares to the current year, so no "time-weighting" misconception yields 50,833. 10(d) writes "90,000 x 6/12 + 270,000 x 6/12 = 180,000 + 7,500". The total of 187,500 is right, but the equation is garbled; it should read 45,000 + 135,000 + 7,500.

issue: The lesson never teaches the control-number rule (income from continuing operations), the treatment of a loss, or contingently issuable shares. Practice items far-eps-14 and far-eps-15 test these. The flowchart's "Start: basic EPS ... Does it lower EPS?" leaves open which EPS line governs.
evidence: Searching lesson.md for "control", "continuing operations" (it appears only in the presentation bullet), "loss" and "contingent" finds no teaching of these rules. Following the lesson in item 14's fact pattern (loss from continuing operations, net income from a gain on discontinued operations), a student would test dilution against net income and include the potential shares. That is wrong under ASC 260-10-45-18/-19.
source: ASC 260-10-45-18 to 45-20 (control number; loss from continuing operations); ASC 260-10-45-48 (contingently issuable shares in diluted EPS)
fix: Add two bullets to "Diluted EPS". First: "The dilution test uses income from continuing operations (the control number). If that is a loss, all potential shares are antidilutive and diluted EPS = basic EPS for every line." Second: "Contingently issuable shares: include in diluted EPS if the conditions would be met if period-end were the end of the contingency period; include in basic EPS only once all conditions are met." Add a key takeaway for the control number.

issue: Sequencing: far-eps sits in unit far-u2 (Area I), long before far-equity (unit far-u8). Convertible bonds are not taught anywhere outside the EPS lesson. No prerequisite is declared, and the lesson gives no primer.

The primer would cover treasury shares (issued but not outstanding), stock dividends and splits (more shares, no resources), cumulative preferred (arrears carry forward) and convertible bonds (holder may exchange for common), linking to far-equity.

issue: Answer cue: all three distractors are absolutes ("Always included", "Never included", "Included only in basic EPS"), and the key is the only conditional. The key's wording "Included if met at period-end" is also looser than the rule.
evidence: cues.md flags absolutes only in distractors a, b and c. Under ASC 260-10-45-48 the test is whether the conditions would be met if the end of the reporting period were the end of the contingency period, and inclusion also requires the shares to be dilutive. The key's wording blurs this.
fix: Reword the key to "Included if the conditions would be met were the period-end the end of the contingency period (if dilutive)". Replace one absolute distractor with a plausible conditional, e.g. "Included only when the condition is probable of being met" or "Included from the date the condition is expected to be met".

issue: Trap labels do not match the misconception, or label the same misconception inconsistently across items. This degrades any misconception analytics.
evidence: 18(b) $4.00 deducts two years of cumulative dividends and is labeled "overgeneralization"; 03(c) labels the same error "wrong-period". 22(d) $5.60 adds the dividend instead of subtracting it and is labeled "distractor-number"; chk1(b) and 18(c) label that error "wrong-sign". "Shares repurchased reported as incremental shares" is labeled "reversed" in 04(d) and 25(b) but "wrong-classification" in 16(d). "Reports basic EPS as diluted" is labeled "partial-computation" in 08(c) and 20(a), "wrong-rule" in far-x1-08(d) and "wrong-classification" in far-x1-32(a).

fix: Use one label per misconception: two years of dividends -> wrong-period; adding a dividend -> wrong-sign; shares repurchased -> partial-computation (or wrong-classification) consistently; basic reported as diluted -> partial-computation consistently.

issue: The stems do not say that the securities and shares were outstanding all year (or that the share figure is a weighted average), and these answers depend on time-weighting.
evidence: 20: "100,000 shares are outstanding" and "convertible bonds with $50,000 of interest" give no period; if the bonds were issued mid-year, the add-back and the shares would be pro-rated. 25: "10,000 options ... average market price $25" gives no outstanding period. 27: "$1,000,000 of 5% bonds converts into 40,000 shares" gives no period. Comparable items 04, 05, 06 and 16 state "outstanding all year".

fix: Add "outstanding all year" (and "weighted-average" for the 100,000 common shares in 20) to each stem.
